You walk up to the group of researchers. Most appear to be students or post-docs, judging by their ages and the slightly manic look of sleep deprivation in their eyes.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam! A moment of your time, please?" One of them, a younger woman with a ponytail and dark circles under her eyes, steps forward. "We've read about you. A captain with resources, vision, and," she checks something written on her palm, "a documented history of supporting scientific advancement. We have an opportunity for you."

text:
She introduces herself as Dr. Elna Rousseau. She and her twin brother Jarn are the project's leads (though you get the impression that's only true because no one more important has noticed). They lead you away from the main thoroughfares to a small laboratory in a quiet corner of the Academy. Inside, in a cradle of machinery in the middle of the room, a geometric shape about a meter across floats, glowing orange. Something about the air near it is wrong. Your inner ear keeps bracing for a fall that never arrives.

"This," Elna says, her hands already halfway into the explanation, "is the Liminality. A bridge between what is and what could be! Fund us properly, and the laws of physics become negotiable."

text:
"Scavengers found it on the edge of the Sector, literally embedded in rock, and eventually it made its way here." Elna shifts uncomfortably. "There's no mention of it in any Domain records we can find. Pretty much everyone tried to figure out what it was, even Coureuse, but after a decade or so of no progress it was dismissed as a curiosity and left to gather dust."

"A curiosity until we got our chance at it," Jarn says, grinning.

text:
"Well, we're not entirely sure. Our best guess is that this, whatever it is, creates a connection between our universe and... something else. Somewhere else. We can exploit that connection to locally change the rules of physics, almost like programming reality," Jarn says. "Our research is still in its early days."

"So far, we know that we need a Linkage, which links something next to the Liminality to a distant object, and an Instruction, which tells the Linkage what to do. For example..."

He tosses you a sheet of metal with a symbol inscribed on it, then flicks a second sheet towards the artifact. The second sheet has a dense mass of symbols, including the one on the first.

You catch it. The second sheet slows as it nears the Liminality and settles into orbit around it. Your own sheet wrenches out of your hands and clangs off the ceiling.

"Voila." Jarn spreads his arms. "Antigravity. One of the first Instructions we managed to get working, using nothing more than a few scribbles on a scrap of metal. Just imagine what we could do next."

text:
"We need funding. A lot of it. You would not believe what this thing eats even sitting idle. If we ran every experiment we wanted, we would bankrupt the Academy inside a cycle." Elna shakes her head.

"But an independent Captain like yourself? Someone with the resources and vision to see the potential here? That could work. We're counting on an investment from you, not just now but in the future. Of course we'd need a down-payment, in addition to ongoing funding. Say 30,000 credits." There are empty ration cartons stacked behind the good equipment.

"But in exchange, we'll use the Liminality to enhance your fleet in ways no one has ever managed! Custom hullmods that do the impossible. You want a ship that can travel back in time? That can shoot missiles that destroy stars? It's yours. Theoretically of course, once we do the research. And of course you'll need to pay the operating costs."

"Thanks again for the credits! Don't tell Elna I said this, but you have no idea how close we were to having to shut everything down," Jarn says. "Now we can get back to work! And also eat real food!"

"And speaking of credits," Jarn continues, "feel free to invest as much as you'd like. The more funding we have, the faster we can give you shiny new toys to play with. You want cooler ships, right? You can also provide some resources directly."

He cuts off as his sister walks into the frame.

text:
From orbit it reads as a colony. Up close the reading falls apart: buildings larger inside than out, corridors that open onto nowhere and everywhere at once, and people who move a little too correctly.

Scans put energy signatures under the crust that climb past every scale the instruments carry. The source is a rift held open from the far side. The research team calls it the wound.

The reality anchors are ready to deploy. All that remains is to get them close enough. Given the defenses already crowding your screens, that will not come cheap.

Liminal_AttackPlanetInteraction
text:
A swarm of twisted frigates comes up to meet you.

As your fleet approaches, most of them turn out to be civilian shuttles, the dregs that weren't deemed worthy of joining the invasion fleets. But they swarm like insects around the wound in reality.

As they get closer, your sensors officer's voice catches. "$PlayerSirOrMadam... those aren't normal shuttles. The weapon mounts... the energy readings... they're drawing power directly from the wound."

Your fleet readies for battle.

A swarm of twisted frigates comes up to meet you.

This swarm is different from the one you faced before. These designs are meant for war. The Servants of the Entity are learning.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam, new hulls. But they still draw power directly from the wound."

script:

SetTextHighlights "Twisted melodies surround you"
Liminal_AttackPlanetInteraction
text:
At first you are relieved to see only a handful of ships. A handful of ships, even capital ships, shouldn't provide much trouble.

And then they draw closer, and you know them. Ships you had thought unique, each the only one of its kind.

Ziggurats. Not just one, but several. And they draw from the wound like everything else you've faced so far.

"How did they..." someone says beside you. "Wasn't it...?"

Twisted melodies surround you, warped by a wrongness you thought you had gotten used to. All around the bridge, heads lift from consoles.

Your fleet readies for battle.

text:
Elna leads you to the Liminality. The tesseract pulses a hard, sullen orange, brighter than you have ever seen it, and the air around it will not hold still. "The bridge is ready," she says quietly. "It will create a temporary connection to the space between dimensions. Once you're through, you'll have to find and destroy the Avatar of the Entity. It's the final tether holding the Entity's connection to our universe."

She hesitates, looking at the distorted space around the Liminality. "Remember what this costs. When we sever this connection, all planets under the Entity's control will be destroyed. There's no way around that. The corruption runs too deep."

"But if we don't do this now," she continues, looking straight at you, "the Entity will only grow stronger. It will dig in deeper and take world after world, until there is no door left to close."

She activates the Liminality, and a swirling portal of orange light opens before you. Through it lies a space your eyes refuse to settle on. The distances there will not agree with themselves, and the horizon folds the wrong way. Far off, a vast shape shifts and writhes, countless hulls fused into a single body that hangs too large for the space around it.

"That's the Avatar," Elna says. "The Entity's manifestation in our universe. Destroy it, and we can finally cut off the connection."

Your fleet readies itself for the final battle.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam! We've had a breakthrough, a big one!" Elna is grinning, but her eyes keep flicking to the readouts even as she talks to you. "The Liminality is responding to our Instructions in ways we never expected. We're seeing patterns in its behavior that suggest it's... learning, adapting to our research."

"You should see the numbers!" Jarn adds. "The Instructions run at half the energy cost they used to. And the Liminality isn't just from another universe, it's actually a Tesseract! A projection of a four-dimensional object into our measly three dimensions. Well, technically everything is a projection of a four-dimensional object, what with time and all, but this is a different kind of projection!"

"Though there are some anomalies," Elna continues, slower now. "Sometimes the Liminality seems to react to Instructions before we even finish writing them. And the energy readings drift even when nothing is running. But that's just part of the learning process, right?"

"Exactly!" Jarn says. "We're rewriting physics faster than we can write it down. A few energy spikes are nothing to worry about."

"$PlayerSirOrMadam, we need to talk," Elna says. "The Liminality's output outgrew our gauges. It outgrew the replacements. And it's started writing Instructions of its own. I think we should stop the research."

"Stop? Now? When we're so close to understanding it?" Jarn looks at her like she's joking. "It's just getting more efficient at helping us! We've done things with physics that no-one even thought could be possible!"

"You're not seeing what I'm seeing," Elna says. She doesn't look up from the readout. "The Instructions it's writing... they're not like ours. I started mapping one this morning. It hasn't ended yet, and I can't find the part that says what it's for."

"You're being paranoid," Jarn says. "The Liminality is a bridge. Bridges don't want things. We control it, not the other way around."

"I hope you're right," Elna says quietly. "But if something does happen... well, I just want to make sure we're ready."

"$PlayerSirOrMadam." Elna stands with her back to the readouts. "The Liminality went unstable. The output climbed past every limit we'd set, and Jarn was recalibrating the cradle. He was too close." She says it evenly. It is not the first time she has had to say it.

"We managed to get control back, but..." She looks at the floating tesseract, which pulses a slow, sullen orange. "It's not just a bridge anymore. Something is coming through. Something called the Entity. Its invasion fleets are already here, taking planets."

"We've detected four staging points, worlds the Entity has... corrupted. Each scan comes back different. Even the coastlines move between passes."

"But we have a chance. In trying to stabilize the Liminality, we've developed reality anchors, devices that force reality back to its own rules. Get them close enough to the centers of the staging grounds and those rifts collapse. The Entity loses its footholds."

text:
"The Entity's ships are drawing power directly from the other dimensions. They're extensions of the Entity's will now. They're Servants of the Entity. Destroying enough of them weakens its connection to our universe, but only for a while. The staging points are what matter." She talks through every attempt to interrupt. No pause is long enough to fit a question about Jarn.

"The longer we wait, the more planets it takes. The fleets don't bomb and don't land troops. A world they touch keeps its cities and its people. A month later the people belong to it, down to how they walk."

"Please..." Her voice breaks. "Jarn believed this research could do good. Prove him right."

"But there's one last thing we need to do," she continues, her voice flattening. "The Entity's connection to our universe isn't completely severed. It's still holding on through the Liminality itself. We need to cut that final thread."
